vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes skip the schedule and the release-age wait, and always carry a release label so check-release-label passes and the fix actually ships.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Changes deployed transitive deps, so it releases like a runtime patch. Manual-tier packages are pinned exactly, so this can't move them.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

customManagers.description: Zerops runtime bases: `base: bun@1.2` (tracked against the same oven/bun images as the Dockerfiles). Zerops only offers some versions, so check before merging.
Single source of truth for the Bun version used by CI (setup-bun reads this file).
zcli version pinned in the zerops-push deploy action.

packageRules.description: Runtime patch bumps, grouped per workspace package. After the catalog migration, deps left in a package's own package.json are only used by that package, so a change that only affects one app lands in that app's PR.
Runtime minor bumps, grouped per workspace package, kept apart from patch so the release label is unambiguous.
In 0.x a 'minor' bump can be breaking (PR #378: @tanstack/ai 0.x). Keep them out of the routine minor group so the safe updates aren't held up by them, and flag the PR.
prBodyNotes: **0.x minor bumps can contain breaking changes.** Read each package's changelog before merging; a green Build/Test doesn't cover much of the app yet.

packageRules.description: Majors are never grouped and wait for approval on the Dependency Dashboard instead of using up PR slots. Manual-tier packages (bottom of this file) override this and always open a PR.
Shared deps defined once in the pnpm-workspace.yaml catalog: one PR updates every consumer. Treated as runtime (release label by update type).
Dev tooling (devDependencies) never ships to users: separate group per package and release:skip, so merging doesn't cut a release or deploy.
Type-only packages, wherever they're declared, behave like dev tooling.
Biome is dev tooling used by every package; one repo-wide PR instead of one per package.
Families whose packages should move together, repo-wide.
One Bun version everywhere: .bun-version (CI), oven/bun images (Docker), bun@ bases (Zerops).
One Node version everywhere: node images (Docker), setup-node (CI), nodejs@ bases (Zerops).
Our own images (built by build-and-deploy.yml) are versioned by our releases, not by Renovate.
Infra services and proxies (Postgres/pgvector, Redis, RustFS, nginx, traefik). A bump can mean a data migration or config change, so these wait for approval on the Dependency Dashboard.
GitHub Actions don't ship to users.
pnpm.overrides are security pins on a specific major (e.g. `undici@^6`). Proposing a new major for them makes no sense; prune them instead.
Dev-only bumps to the published CLI must not publish a new npm version (publish-cli.yml defaults to a patch release for any packages/cli change).
Same for the published Paseo plugin.
apps/landing is excluded from the CI build (pre-existing shiki/rolldown WASM failure), so a green check proves nothing for it.
The create-integration scaffold template isn't installed or tested; refresh it monthly in one PR so new integrations don't start on stale versions.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: MANUAL TIER. Packages whose updates can need code or schema changes. They still open a PR on the normal schedule, majors included, but each family gets its own PR (never mixed with routine updates), a needs-migration label and a checklist. Pinned to exact versions so lockfile maintenance can't move them without a PR.
prBodyNotes:
**Manual tier: Better Auth.** Before merging:
- [ ] Read the changelog for every package in this PR.
- [ ] Run `npx @better-auth/cli generate --output /tmp/auth-schema.ts` and compare its tables/columns with `packages/database/schema/auth.ts` (the real schema; `packages/auth/auth-schema.ts` is a stale copy).
- [ ] If anything is missing, update `schema/auth.ts`, run `pnpm -F @repo/database generate` and commit the migration.
- [ ] Smoke-test sign-in (GitHub + Doras), 2FA, passkeys, API keys and the MCP/OAuth consent flow locally.

**Manual tier: Drizzle.** Before merging:
- [ ] Read the changelog (0.x: minors can break).
- [ ] Run `pnpm -F @repo/database generate` and confirm it produces no unexpected migration or snapshot-format churn.
- [ ] Run `pnpm -F @repo/database migrate` against a local database.

**Manual tier: Polar.** Before merging:
- [ ] Check whether the dated API entrypoints we import (e.g. `@polar-sh/sdk/2026-10`) still exist or have a newer version to move to.
- [ ] Test checkout, seat changes and the Polar webhook locally.

**Manual tier: TanStack Start/Router.** Before merging:
- [ ] Read the changelog.
- [ ] Run `pnpm -F start dev`, check that the route tree regenerates cleanly, and click through admin and the public portal.

**Manual tier: TanStack AI** (0.x, and the core and adapters must match). Before merging:
- [ ] Check every `@tanstack/ai*` package is on a mutually compatible version.
- [ ] Test AI task summaries locally.

**Manual tier: ProseKit/ProseMirror.** prosemirror-* versions are also pinned in root `pnpm.overrides`; keep them in step. Before merging:
- [ ] Test the editor (tasks, comments, mentions, images, code blocks) and markdown rendering in the worker.

**Manual tier: discord.js.** Before merging:
- [ ] Read the changelog and run the Discord bot against a test server.

packageRules.description: zcli is deploy tooling: a bump doesn't change the app, so it shouldn't cut a release. Review it, since it changes how every deploy runs.
